name: Founding of South-View Cemetery
description: A group of Black civic and church leaders in Atlanta established South-View Cemetery so that African Americans could be buried with dignity and respect, free from the segregated and neglected conditions of existing city cemeteries.

name: Atlanta Race Massacre of 1906
description: A violent white-supremacist attack that swept through Atlanta over four days in September 1906. Mobs destroyed Black businesses, homes, and attacked Black residents. The massacre reshaped the city's racial geography and deepened community solidarity.

name: Atlanta Black Voter Registration Drives
description: Sustained campaigns to register Black voters in Atlanta and Fulton County. Led by civic leaders like John Wesley Dobbs, these drives transformed Atlanta's political landscape and helped elect the city's first moderate white mayors.

name: Founding of Atlanta Life Insurance Company
description: Alonzo Herndon purchased a failing mutual aid association and built it into Atlanta Life Insurance Company, which became one of the largest Black-owned businesses in the nation and a pillar of Auburn Avenue's economic ecosystem.

name: Auburn Avenue Golden Era
description: Auburn Avenue, known as 'Sweet Auburn,' became the richest Black street in America. It was home to Black-owned businesses, churches, newspapers, and cultural institutions that anchored Atlanta's African American community.

name: Black Workers' Labor Movement in Atlanta
description: Black workers organized across trades — Pullman porters, domestic workers, garment workers — demanding fair wages and safer conditions. These labor efforts connected to broader national movements for Black economic justice.
